verdict.rationale: Lium's first-party docs and CLI cover the whole agent loop without a browser: rent by spec through the API or `lium up`, run workloads with `lium exec` (which returns the remote exit code), and remove pods automatically via TTL or spend cap or by the SDK after the run. Monitoring is evidenced mainly as spend tracking (`lium spend`) plus running `nvidia-smi` through exec. The OpenAPI probe 404s only hit docs.lium.io paths, while the documented schema lives at lium.io/api/openapi.json, so they are not a contradiction. missing for 10: a documented pod status/health-monitoring endpoint or command beyond spend tracking, and independent hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end flow.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
lium exec job "nvidia-smi"                              # exits with the remote command's exit code
The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
rent-by-spec (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) that rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
lium spend                                     # burn per hour, spend per pod, runway
